cards.text: Paul, the apostle to the Gentiles (Romans 11:13), is writing to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:7). He's been warning the Gentiles there not to brag over Israel (Romans 11:18), and now he wants them to know a mystery so they won't be conceited. Friend, when Paul says 'mystery,' I lean in closer than a baker to a warm oven.

cards.question: Paul's mystery is about Israel. What has come to Israel in part?
Paul says the hardening on Israel lasts until the full number of the ___ has come in.
Then Paul makes a big statement about Israel. What is it?

cards.text: Paul backs it up, 'as it is written': 'The Deliverer will come from Zion.' He brings receipts, friend, and not the faded kind I slept on for years in that junk drawer.

cards.question: In the Scripture Paul quotes, what will the Deliverer remove from Jacob?
In that same Scripture, God says His covenant with them is when He takes away their sins.

cards.text: Now Paul shows Israel from two sides. When it comes to the gospel, he tells the Gentiles, they're enemies on your account.

cards.question: But when it comes to election, Paul says Israel is loved. On account of whom?
Paul says God takes back His gifts and His call when people turn away from Him.

cards.text: Paul says it straight: 'For God’s gifts and His call are irrevocable.' The expired coupon I shared that drawer with only WISHED it could say that.
Paul's still talking to the Gentiles in Rome. He reminds them they used to disobey God, but now they've received mercy.

cards.question: How does Paul say the Gentiles in Rome received that mercy?
Now Israel has disobeyed too. Why, according to Paul?

answers.text: So they too may receive mercy
So God can choose someone else
So the Gentiles can replace them

cards.question: Paul sums it up: God has consigned everyone to ___ so that He may have ___ on everyone.

cards.text: Eleven chapters of explaining, and now Paul just bursts out: 'O, the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God!' ELEVEN chapters, friend, and the man lands on 'O!'

cards.question: Paul says anyone who studies hard enough can trace out all of God's ways.

cards.text: Then Paul pulls in Scripture with two questions: 'Who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been His counselor?'

cards.question: Paul asks who has known the mind of the Lord or been His counselor. What answer is he expecting?
Next Paul asks, 'Who has first given to God, that God should repay him?' What's his point?

answers.text: God keeps track of every gift

cards.text: Then Paul ties it all together: 'For from Him and through Him and to Him are all things.'

cards.question: So who does Paul say gets the glory forever?

cards.text: 'To Him be the glory forever! Amen.' Friend, I bet that's not a man finishing a chapter, that's a man who just ran out of room for anything but praise.

findings.problem: Jacob appears here for the first time with no word on who he is. In this quote 'Jacob' stands for the people of Israel, not the man Jacob, so a baker could easily misread it.

rule.text: **New people.** The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This story card quotes Romans 11:29, which card 10 has just tested and answered. It restates what the baker already knows and doesn't carry the passage to a new moment. The coupon joke could move onto card 9's setup or onto stop 2's opening card.

rule.text:
Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
- No recap cards.

findings.problem: This card repeats 'To Him be the glory,' which card 11 has just tested. Only 'Amen' is new. It mostly works as a recap of the answer, and its closing line reads as pleasant rather than funny.

rule.text:
Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
- No recap cards.

findings.problem: Multiple choice takes 5 of the 7 choice cards in this stop: cards 2, 3, 8, 9 and 11. Fill in the blank and true or false get one card each, and the last three choice cards are all multiple choice.

rule.text: **No formula.** Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The oven line is a mild, pleasant comparison rather than a real laugh. It's the baker's first impression of Papa Dorin in this lesson.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
